definitions.explanation: The amount of salary actually received after taxes and other deductions; what you actually get in your hands.

examples.japanese: {手取|てど}り⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦いくら→いくら：00943_ikura⟧⟦もらっています→もらう：00520_morau⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
examples.english: How much do you take home?
The gross is 300,000 yen, but the take-home is about 250,000.

examples.japanese: {手取|てど}り20⟦{万円|まんえん}→万円：09900_manen⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{生活|せいかつ}する→生活する：01839_seikatsusuru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{大変|たいへん}→大変：00594_taihen⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: It's hard to live on a take-home pay of 200,000 yen.

examples.japanese: {手取|てど}り⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ふ}える→増える：01183_fueru⟧⟦ように→ように：10081_youni⟧⟦{節税|せつぜい}→節税：16469_setsuzei⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I'm doing tax planning to increase my take-home pay.

notes:
{手取|てど}り literally means "what you take in hand" - the actual amount you receive.

ETYMOLOGY:
⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧ (hand) + ⟦{取|と}り→取る：00565_toru⟧ (taking) - what you actually take into your hands.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {手取|てど}り⟦で→で：00502_de⟧〜⟦{円|えん}→円：00774_en⟧ - 〜 yen take-home
- {手取|てど}り⟦{給料|きゅうりょう}→給料：01086_kyuuryou⟧ - take-home salary
- {手取|てど}り⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{少|すく}ない→少ない：01136_sukunai⟧ - take-home is low

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {手取|てど}り vs. ⟦{額面|がくめん}→額面：07073_gakumen⟧: {手取|てど}り is net (after deductions); ⟦{額面|がくめん}→額面：07073_gakumen⟧ is gross (before deductions)
- {手取|てど}り vs. ⟦{総支給額|そうしきゅうがく}→総支給額：noentry⟧: ⟦{総支給額|そうしきゅうがく}→総支給額：noentry⟧ is the total amount paid; {手取|てど}り is what you receive

USAGE NOTE:
When discussing salaries in Japan, people often refer to {手取|てど}り rather than ⟦{額面|がくめん}→額面：07073_gakumen⟧ since this reflects the actual usable income. Common deductions include income tax, resident tax, health insurance, and pension contributions.
